items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the detective story 'The Case of the Fifth Word', and answer.

"The note on the library desk had only seven words: 'Look where the fifth word points tonight.' Kavya read it twice, then pulled the old encyclopedia from the shelf. 'Points,' she murmured. 'Maybe it means an entry, not a direction.' She turned to the fifth word of the note and began to search."

Answer the following:
(i) How many words did the note have?  (a) Ten  (b) Seven  (c) Six  (d) Five
(ii) Which book did Kavya take from the shelf?
(iii) What new meaning of "points" did Kavya consider?
(iv) Which quality of a detective does Kavya show?  (a) Impatience  (b) Carelessness  (c) Careful, logical thinking – considering other meanings of a word  (d) Fear
items.answer: (i) (b) Seven (ii) The old encyclopedia. (iii) That it could mean pointing to an entry in a book rather than a direction. (iv) (c) Careful, logical thinking – considering other meanings of a word
items.markingKey: (i) (b) Seven (ii) The old encyclopedia. (iii) That it could mean pointing to an entry in a book rather than a direction. (iv) (c) Careful, logical thinking – considering other meanings of a word (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
